name: Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition

data: Very fun and beautiful game, with an excellent story and soundtrack
10/10 - made me cry, the music and art alone is well worth playing
Amazing story, amazing graphics, amazing gameplay and an amazing soundtrack
My only complaint is that the game can become difficult
The combat in this game is garbage, very boring and tedious
the section feels tedious and frustrating since I don't feel like I have control over my character
And the run at the end of the game is so punishing it's just not fun
, I don't find the platforming to be that fun, and I think the combat is the least appealing aspect of this game
also the combat is straight cheeks
during the gameplay I was cursing everyone made the game and I had to come here rant because of it, it's that terrible
sharper character movement would have at least made the weird level layout somewhat bearable
I thought I could get past the sappy children's story
I found a lot of things wrong with the game and considered writing a negative review
the deaths feel cheap, the enemy design feels cheap, everything feels like a chore, frustrating rather than challenging
challenge is not the point for this game
Their answer to poor balancing of the platforming challenge at certain points is to essentially add a built in save-scumming feature

This has to be hands down the prettiest game I've played in my entire life. Gameplay is smooth and somewhat challenging, making the progress feel that much more rewarding, while the environments and the soundtrack immensely help deliver a story that feels like a match made in heaven.
I really have nothing but praise for this one, and I can't possibly recommend it highly enough.
This game is amazing. I got it for 75% off and now feel like I didn't pay enough for it.

Absolutely gorgeous game, superb soundtrack, touching story, and extremely frustrating spikes that will murder you all rolled up into a wonderful little game! Definitely one of my favourites now, wish I had of known about it when it released. Onward's to Ori and the Will of the Wisps!

This game feels like a combination of Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze and Rayman: Origins to me, which is to say a combination of two good games. Great story telling and overall experience as well. I'm interested in playing the second game.

I have been a gamer for more years than I can remember and I have never come across a 2D game as beautiful, enigmatic and well developed as Ori and the blind forest.
Everything about this game is marvellous. The graphics are incredible, the soundtrack is beautiful, the gameplay is smooth, and the story is overwhelmingly good, sad, beautiful and exciting all at the same time.
If you want to play a mindblowing game, then do not think about buying this game... JUST GO FOR IT.
My girlfriend is not a gamer because she gets bored, but when I played Ori, she would just sit next to me the whole time and get anxious, stressed, happy or even sad while watching little Ori and his/her adventures.
We LOVE this game.

While the game is cute, well made and has great music but it is beyond annoying. I do not recommend this game unless you are a platform fanatic and have the reflexes of a 7 year old. My only saving grace is that I got it on a big discount. If you think im kidding, I was probably around 20% into the game before I got sick of it and yet ONLY 49% OF PLAYERS HAVE THE ACHIEVEMENT for where i was up to. That means half of all players didnt even make it to where I did before quitting. Tells you ALOT.
Ori is a good game marred with bad controls. I really wanted to like it, but the controls left me frustrated and angry.
A beautiful and fun game. Metroidvania, with a positive, aesthetic and creative twist. Great for young and old. A touching story that will leave you in tears. A work of art.

I loved this game. I actually got the sequel first, Will Of The Wisps, & that game is absolutely one of my favorite games ever. Now, while this game was fun, I do prefer Will Of The Wisps. It's just a more polished game, & the save system doesn't give me a headache.
If you liked Will Of The Wisps, you'll probably like this game (though it's certainly more punishing)
If you liked this game, you'll LOVE Will Of The Wisps.
Still a great game with fun combat, tricky platforming, & a touching story.

This is a lovely game with absolutely gorgeous music and graphics, a sweet story, and really responsive controls for a very agile character. It doesn't take a whole lot of time to play (easily 100% it in a few hours once you know where everything is) but is a lot of fun and has enough little hidden places and new environments to hold interest. I'll play it sometimes just to bounce around the pathways without touching the ground, just because I can! I look forward to the sequel.

When looking back on side-scrolling platformers like Rayman and Megaman it's hard to find a favorite. Even more difficult is finding a current-day equivalent to their master works. Ori is gorgeous... Enough said... Just buy it and be happy. This review is done.

It's beauty is in the atmosphere it creates. A primal world that is dying and Ori is the last of her kind to save it. The voices (though there are only two you really hear) are beautifully mastered and really give it that elegant and "spirit-like" feel. The environment flows beautifully and practically (you won't get caught on the environment from some random invisible wall). The controls are tight and intuitive, but using them smoothly takes practice.

Definitely a game worth buying, and worth the continuity with the sequel on its way. I'm especially happy that the creator of AM2R is working on it who has the understanding and passion for side-scrolling platformers as Moon Studios.

The art style and music are beautiful and I really like the game mechanics, but either I am exceptionally bad at this game (possible) or it is way too easy to accidentally wander into an area you aren't prepared for and become trapped there.

I've had to start from scratch three times because I ended up in an area where I couldn't progress because I either didn't have the nescessary skills yet or the correct number of energy cells and I couldn't escape to go get those things (lookin' at you Moon Grotto...)

An extremely emotive, visually vivid, and aurally appealing Metroidvania with intermittently insane difficulty spikes.

B+

Gorgeous game, beautiful sound track and effects, fluid animation, rich control set, awesome platforming. Platforming sequences serve as set pieces, where they are the "boss fights", there aren't any actual boss characters to fight. Platforming difficulty ranges from pretty easy to very challenging, looking at the leader boards, I thought I was the only one, but it's typical to have over 600 deaths upon game completion, the top person had over 800 deaths. While that suggests how challenging the game can get, it's also due to how easy it is to immediately try again after death, the save mechanism on this is just a great idea.

I played this using a Playstation controller, but I think this will play well using KBM, maybe in some parts easier for many of the chain target-propel jumps.

Although the game starts off a little slow, it picks up quick enough. The story mainly deals with love and loss, not the romantic sort of love, but familial, and bonds of friendship.

honestly its a fun game and the mechanics are pretty good i think the moon company has always done pretty well with the story telling part of the game, the enemies aren't really hard to read and there isn't a specific hard enemy to maneuver, although if you're a trophy addict then some of the missions might be hard to complete i know when i tried playing one life i for sure questioned my life. i would say this game is really well balanced preferred over the second one

Can you believe that this game has a sequel that's even better? I'm playing it and I still can't believe it. I'm actively kicking myself for not having played this masterpiece sooner. It's a once-in-a-lifetime experience to play it without any spoilers for the first time, and oh gosh the way it looks on an OLED screen, aaaaaaaaaaaa!
One of the best metroidvania I´ve ever played. Visualy is a piece of art, soundtrack is absolutely fantastic and a very emotional story that make this game an unmissable experiencie.
This game is one of the most captivating games I've ever played. The graphics are gorgeous, the storyline is awesome, and the gameplay is so much fun. Highly reccomend this game.
beautiful scenery and vibes, i loved the game mechanics and abilities, the story is good, anyone would understand it and like it.

Definitely recommend this game to everyone! Even my wife, who isn't a gamer, enjoyed watching me play it and tried the controller herself! A visually stunning masterpiece with a compelling story. Can't wait to play the sequel! This game is worth every second I spent playing it.
Amazing metroidvania, even if it is a few years already, sad story but worth playing it to the end.

Pretty damn good game. Very intriguing story and fun platformer. Goes on 75% sale fairly often too

Also playable on Linux using Proton

By far one of my favorite games, great story, great concept. I strongly recomend getting this game. You will love it!
10/10 | 5 stars

Have you ever cried tears of joy while playing a video game before? Perhaps not.

Do you want to? This is the game that will do it.

I don't usually like platformer however there's something in this game that keep me playing. Either it's the amazing visual style, breathtaking soundtrack, satisfying control, level design, or the captivating story, Ori is simply an amazing game.

10 years later and this game is still just as beautiful as I remember ♡

... My skill level, however, has gotten noticeably worse! This game isn't the trickiest by any means, but still requires a good degree of patience and practice. How on earth it's possible to complete with just one life is absolutely beyond me. I'm proud of my game completion with 300+ deaths, thank you for asking!
As far as platformers go this is top tier. Great story, 10/10 soundtrack. Fantastic gameplay. very smoothe and fun to play. Repetative as well. What a game!

Pleasant looking environments and vivid visual effects.

The game ramps up smoothy from basic things, like jumping and attacking, to more complex timing and acrobatics. Never got stuck, never ran into bugs. The game keeps rewarding you for backtracking and using your new powers in other places, and there are plenty of shortcuts to unlock. The music score is soothing, but also has plenty of appropriate tracks for escape sequences and dramatic moments. The majority of escape portions of each dungeon come down to memorization and repeated failure, which may disappoint some. The game has some surprises to mix things up, like an object you can hold to walk up walls.

The checkpoint system is very forgiving and flexible, letting you place one as long as you have the power and you're standing on something solid away from enemies.

If you like games like Metroid, but with nature visuals, more puzzles, and a lack of bosses, it's worth a look.

11/10 would cry again
This is one of my favorite games of all time and I can't wait for the sequel.
The soundtrack is phenomenal, the controls are tight and precise. The world and characters are endearing and beautifully designed to the point where sometimes I'll just get distracted from playing by how awesome the backgrounds look. Yes, its hard, but its worth it.
I love this game and I absolutely recommend picking it up, it's definitely worth the full price.

Overall fantastic game - Beautiful soundtrack, art, and game design. It's a movement based platformer with emphasis on story-telling. It has thought-provoking puzzles, challenging platforming sections, and plenty of areas to explore. I'm working on a second playthrough and I've already found so much that I missed when I first played it. It's truly a masterpiece that anyone can enjoy, whether you love puzzles, exploring, or are new to gaming.

The short summary: 11/10
At its core, it's a simple platforming adventure. But stunning visuals, masterful music, and fluid controls make this game a masterpiece and a prime example of video games as a form of art. A brilliant game I didn't take the time to play for far too long.

The full review:
The platforming formula is nothing new to the gaming industry, but Ori and the Blind Forest stands out from the crowd thanks to it's gorgeous visuals and atmospheric music. Ori controls smoothly and intuitively, and as you gain new abilities and achieve objectives, more of the labyrinth-like forest becomes accessible to you. Secrets abound, but not so much that it's tedious to uncover them all, and a healthy challenge on Normal difficulty. The adventure is short and the story simple, yet it is told in a manner that doesn't impede gameplay nor require walls of dialogue.

I absolutely love this game. I fell in love with it by the time the prologue concluded and found its story to be mesmerizing despite its relative simplicity. There's enough of an enigma to be intriguing and has left me excited to set forth into the sequel.

If you have any interest in platformer adventure games, please give this one a try. Ori and the Blind Forest may be an older game, but it's a fantastic game and well worth the few hours it takes to play through it.

Awesome game.
Probably the best platformers out (at least a must play).
Amazing visuals, solid gameplay and mechanics as well as a great story (that is told without making you feel like you keep getting taken out of the action).
The character design is awesome too, enemies are organic and remensisent of the real world but with an Ori slant; and often make up part of the 'puzzle' elements themselves. Ori (the lil' avatar you actually play) is next level, you can move like a ninja, attack multiple enemies at once - all in smooth and intuitive manner. Ori's personality is evident in every movement and makes you feel like the ultimate squirrely badarse.

You should definately play this game.
Awesome for platformers and those who have never played a platformer alike; it's just really well done.
An amazing platformer, some stages can be annoying but, fortunately the game lets you solve the puzzles your way.
This game is amazing, from the sound track, platforming and the graphics that still hold up to this day, worth the money, and a complete steal if you get it on special. You must play this game.

Its a good game with beautiful graphics and an interesting story. My only problem is the fact I have no idea where I'm going. Nor do I know if I'm supposed to come back once I've gotten certain abilities or anything else like that. My sense of direction is awful, yet I have an easier time navigating Hollow Knight than I do this. But getting lost is half the fun to me.

Needless to say, if you get frustrated with not having a set direction to go, this game is gonna frustrate you greatly.
Although not as polished and as diverse as the sequel, this is still an excellent game with interesting core gameplay and a compelling story.

The story is really cool and the art is absolutely gorgeous along with the sound track!

Now there are some frustrating parts about this game, but it’s mostly me being bad at using a controller (I play with an Xbox controller).

There’s two parts of the game that super stressed me out, but it’s mostly because i get super stressed when I’m on a time limit and basically have to rush to exit that part of the game. I don’t have enough time to take the path in and have to die over and over till I get it down and get a clear picture of where I should go/what I should do to get past these parts. But like I said it was only twice! Other than that the game is pretty chill and the combat is super easy~

Overall it’s very beautiful, fun, and challenging!

I don't know why, but I really dislike this one. I'm a huge Metroidvania fan and was really looking forward to this one, but I just do not enjoy playing it. I think the issue is the gameplay sits somewhere between metroidvania and precision platforming, the latter of which I can't stand playing. I find a lot of the minute-to-minute gameplay here extremely frustrating with insta-kill spikes everywhere, bullet-sponge enemies, and really bland combat - at least in the early game. I really don't have the patience to push through the game any longer.

everything to say about this game has been said.. it's beautiful. I'm amazed how it can give you an emotional rollercoaster by such a simple scenario. makes me admire once more, how powerful storytelling can be.

The soundtrack of the game is awesome. I discovered this game the last E3 with the announcement of the second part, so I gave it a chance to this game and it was an incredible adventure. Hope to see the next part soon.

10/10

The game.
The only game which made me fall in love with platform games again.

This game is something full of emotions right from sadness to happiest.
From "Aww! Poor Ori." to "Kill them filthy creatures!"

Absolute beauty of a game. Just enough difficulty to get me to keep learning until the end, not terribly long (half my time was probably idled for cards/pause menu), and the story broke my heart. It tells things through slight narration and atmosphere, as well as emotional characters. Definitely worth the time.

(I am not a profession reviewer, sorry for the short paragraph)
Amazing game. The story, gameplay, music, visuals were all 10/10. I got it for $20 and it was worth every penny.

Edit after getting all the achievements : Astounding graphics and overall exploration, could be tedious without the dash skill unless you enjoy the visuals and going around the map. An awesome experience the first time you play it, though, if you're aiming for full achievements, then good luck.

About the Unhinged achievement
Be careful if you die while playing One Life mode, as there's a bug which seems to change the difficulty of the savegame after you respawn. If you complete the game on that same savegame even though it says Difficulty: One Life mode , you won't get the achievement. If you die, better delete the savegame, make a new one and try again, just to be safe.

I originally played this game on Xbox on release and thoroughly enjoyed myself despite this not being the typical game I play. A year or so later I decided to purchase the definitive version on PC to play again as I never played the DLC the first time around. The game is just as good, a high quality metroidvania with excess fat on it. Because of that it is not the longest game (I played 16 hours getting every item) but that is because it never wastes your time with the standard filler that is in so many games today. The graphics are great, the gameplay is fun and tight, and combined they produce a great experience.

Such a good game. The movement is perfect. How they slowly introduce new skills until you're a master of movement- by the end of the game you're so capable. Beautiful visuals and storytelling. Gave me goosebumps a couple times. Such a welcome relief from the content dump games that take 100s of hours.

That's amazing! I've been looking for reason to play this game again sometime (i can't play the same game twice without any change), and here it is! I love it. I love the story, characters, music, graphics - everything in this game is amazing. Atmosphere feels like a fairy-tale... Well, maybe because it is?
Defenitely worth playing.

P.S.
(possible spoiler) I was gladly surprised, when falling down from Sorrow pass frog made a wilhelm scream :D

...in a world of shadows, Ori came to help the light to come back.

Ori and the Blind Forest is a great Plattformer.
Plenty of enemys, big map with lots of things to explore and a feeling you wont get on other games.

The overall game is pretty good. Nice controls, godlike music and the look of the game is stunning.
Best 20€ i´ve spend on Steam.

Your run-of-the-mill platformer, enjoyable but nothing too special.

Pros: generally pretty, main character is very well animated, chill music, interesting save system, powerful and satisfying endgame powers, decent world you will wanna explore in the endgame

Cons: sometimes confusing visuals. sluggish earlygame, not always clear where to go, "interesting" save system can make you stuck for a long time, abrupt ending, horrible (HORRENDOUS!) MKB controls, rage inducing (in a bad way) escape sequences

This game will always have a place in my heart. I will eventually replay this when I've gotten through my backlogs. I played this after Hollow Knight, so I had some expectations going into the game, and they were all blown away. While the movements didn't feel as crisp as Hollow Knight, it didn't need to be. It would not have fit into this game world. The story though, ugh my heart. And don't get me started on the visuals of this game, as you could probably already tell from the trailer. It's. Incredible. Beautiful. Beautiful is the bare minimum term to describe this game. I've never played a game as unique as this, and I still haven't found one yet if I don't count its sequel.

tldr.text: Very Positive (94%): players love the art, graphics and story.
Combat and gameplay draw the most complaints.

details.text: Recent reviews are about as positive as the all-time score, so the game still holds up for buyers today.
Reviews from players with under 2 hours are 76% positive, against 98% from players with over 50 hours, so newer players are far less won over.
